evidence: Reviewer correctly spotted that after moving the bg/fg cascade upstream, applySegmentLayout's own synthesized pad/marker cells got a null Style. Verified via commit 3febf5a: it adds a baseStyle option threaded only into truncateCells/padCells's `new StripCell(..., baseStyle)` calls for synthesized cells, leaving existing cells' own style untouched -- exactly the fix the reviewer proposed.
guidance_note: When moving a style cascade upstream to preserve fragment-level styling, audit every remaining site that still constructs StripCells directly (padding, truncate markers) for the same style requirement before opening the PR.

evidence: Reviewer identified that merging baseStyle into fragments before grouping produces parts-based cells whose truncation-time rebuild (`new StripCell(slice, cell.style)`) drops style. Agent chose the reviewer's own suggested option A -- collapsing uniform-style fragment groups into a single-text cell -- and backed it with a byte-equivalence test proving the serializer coalesces adjacent same-SGR segments identically either way.
guidance_note: When introducing a parts-based cell shape, decide the truncation/slicing strategy for it in the same change and prove byte-equivalence for any shape-collapsing optimization before merging, rather than discovering the gap across two more review rounds.

evidence: F2's collapse only handles uniform-style fragment groups; genuinely heterogeneous per-fragment fg (the gitTaculous shape this very PR migrates) still produces parts-based cells that truncation can cut through, dropping per-part fg since StripCell._parts is private. The agent picked the reviewer's own third suggested option (document the limitation) rather than the structural fix, confirmed no current segment configures fixed-width truncation over heterogeneous fg, pinned two tests, and filed a follow-up ticket with a concrete resolution sketch -- a reasonable deferral of a currently-theoretical gap rather than premature complexity.
guidance_note: When a style-collapse optimization only covers the common (uniform) case, say explicitly in the same commit which shapes remain exposed to the surrounding operation (truncation) instead of leaving that for the next review round to find.

evidence: The test added by F2's fix (3febf5a, in test/segment-cells.test.ts) was named/commented as proving byte-equivalence to a parts-based cell but only asserted visible text plus 'at least one SGR sequence' -- confirmed a71a3be (the intervening round-2 fix commit) never touched this test file, so the gap sat in F2's original test since round 0. The agent's round-3 fix built an explicit parts-based StripCell and asserted equal rendered bytes, which now actually enforces the claim.
guidance_note: When a test's name or comment asserts an exact-equivalence claim, write the assertion that actually performs that comparison in the same commit, not a proxy check (visible text, 'has an SGR code').

narrative: The redesign moved default bg/fg styling upstream to preserve per-fragment fg under a segment background; the reviewer caught two real style-loss risks in code the PR itself introduced (synthesized layout cells, and parts-based cells produced by the new upstream merge), both fixed cleanly and verified against the rendered bytes. One residual gap in truncating genuinely heterogeneous parts-based cells was correctly deferred with documentation, pinning tests, and a follow-up ticket rather than force-fitting a structural fix for a theoretical case. The one truly avoidable round was a test (added by the round-0 fix) whose name overclaimed byte-equivalence without actually checking it.
guidance_observations: Deferring the truncation-through-heterogeneous-parts gap with documentation, pinning tests, and a follow-up ticket was the right call given no live segment triggers it, and avoided a [LAW:no-mode-explosion] risk from a defensive general fix.
The one avoidable round traces to a test whose docstring claimed more than its assertion checked -- write the comparison the docstring promises in the same commit the test is added.

evidence: STATE_VALIDATORS was a plain object keyed by an untrusted wire key, so "__proto__"/"constructor" resolve to prototype values and crash the validator call (RENDER_FAILED instead of BAD_REQUEST). Verified via commit 4c2c783's patch: STATE_VALIDATORS and VERBS were both converted from Record/Object.freeze to `new Map(...)`, and lookups switched to `.get(key)`, which eliminates the prototype chain entirely -- stronger than the reviewer's suggested Object.create(null) guard.
guidance_note: Key a lookup table by untrusted wire input with a Map (or Object.create(null)) from the start -- a plain object/Record literal keyed by attacker-controlled strings is a prototype-pollution surface by construction.

evidence: Same prototype-pollution defect as F1, on validateStateWrite's own lookup. Confirmed by the same 4c2c783 patch: `STATE_VALIDATORS.get(key)` replaces the bracket-access, closing this exact code path too.

Same prototype-pollution defect on the VERBS dispatch table. Confirmed by 4c2c783's index.ts patch: VERBS is now `new Map([...])` with `VERB_NAMES` built from `.keys()`, so an unknown/reserved verb string is an ordinary miss rather than a prototype hit.

Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 4c2c783, but that commit's index.ts patch only converts VERBS to a Map -- it never touches setState's key-splitting logic, which traces unchanged to the original round-0 commit (6b5267f); the flag is a false positive, this is a fresh finding on original code, not a fix-caused regression. The reviewer's request (detect `slash === 0` and throw a distinct "empty key" message) is exactly what 928dbe0 implements.
guidance_note: Structurally distinct malformed-input shapes (missing key+value, missing value separator, empty key) deserve their own diagnostic from the first pass, not a generic fallthrough into the unknown-key rejection.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 4c2c783, but 4c2c783's state-validators.ts patch never touches this header comment; the false claim ("Tests assert against this table directly") was written when the file was created in round 0 (6b5267f) and simply resurfaced on a later full-file pass -- a false positive on the flag. The agent made the claim true rather than weakening it, adding test/state-validators.test.ts in 928dbe0 with direct assertions against STATE_KEYS and cross-checks against listResolvablePaletteNames()/STYLE_ORDER.
guidance_note: Don't write "tests assert against this table directly" before those tests exist -- add the comment and the test in the same commit.

evidence: The exhaustiveness test added by F5's fix (928dbe0) hardcoded the palette name "textual-dark" just to obtain a sample ValidateResult, coupling a union-shape test to unrelated registry contents. Confirmed via e0b96d3's patch: the sample is now `listResolvablePaletteNames()[0]`, matching the reply's claim exactly.
guidance_note: Derive incidental sample values for a type-shape test from the same registry under test, not a hardcoded literal, so an unrelated rename can't break the test.

evidence: The reply-hint says "pushback" but the actual reply is a full acceptance with a concrete fix -- a clear reply-hint/verdict mismatch. Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 928dbe0, but that commit's file list never includes state-validators.ts, so the three-way disagreement (comment says four inputs, error lists four, BOOLEAN_FALSY accepts a fifth: "") is a pre-existing defect from 6b5267f, not caused by 928dbe0; false positive on the flag. Confirmed via e0b96d3's patch: BOOLEAN_FALSY drops "" (`new Set(["0", "false"])`), matching the reviewer's offered "remove support" option exactly.
guidance_note: When a comment enumerates "N canonical inputs," make the accepted-set, the comment, and the error message the same literal set from the start -- a convenience inclusion (accepting "" as falsy) shouldn't silently outnumber the documented set.

evidence: The "ValidateResult discriminant is exhaustive" test and its claim of pinning the union at the exhaustiveness check were introduced by F5's fix (928dbe0) and only ever did runtime if/else branching -- confirmed unchanged in that respect by e0b96d3 (F6's fix touched only the sample-derivation line). Verified 0b62099's patch: it replaces the branch with a `checkShape` helper ending in `const _exhaustive: never = s`, which fails `pnpm typecheck` (not Jest) if the union grows a third arm -- the comment now matches what the test actually enforces.
guidance_note: When a test's docstring claims a compile-time invariant, implement it as a `never`-typed assertion in the same commit as the claim, not a runtime if/else that only exercises the union's current members.

evidence: Flagged ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT e0b96d3, but e0b96d3's state-validators.ts patch only touches the BOOLEAN_FALSY set/comment; validateTheme's per-call `listResolvablePaletteNames()` + `.includes()` is unchanged since 6b5267f -- false positive on the flag, this is a fresh perf finding on original code. Confirmed via 0b62099's patch: it adds module-init `RESOLVABLE_THEMES_LIST`/`RESOLVABLE_THEMES`(Set)/`RESOLVABLE_STYLES`(Set) built once, with validateTheme/validateStyle switched to `.has()`, exactly as claimed.
guidance_note: Cache both the accepted-list and its Set at module init when a validator reads a static registry on every call -- do it when the validator is first written, not after review flags the reallocation.

evidence: F7's fix (e0b96d3) tightened BOOLEAN_FALSY to reject "", but the PR description still documented the original looser contract (""/false/0 all accepted as falsy) until this round-4 finding caught the drift. Verified via `gh pr view 31`: the current description's toolbar-expanded row now reads "Empty input is rejected with BAD_REQUEST", matching the reply's claimed edit.
guidance_note: When a fix changes documented input behavior (accept vs. reject), grep the PR description for the old wording and update it in the same commit as the code change, not when a later review round flags the mismatch.

narrative: Round 0 found a genuine three-point prototype-pollution defect, fixed thoroughly by converting both registries to ReadonlyMap rather than patching each object literal -- the strongest available fix, not just the suggested guard. Several later findings (F4, F5, F7, F9) carried ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags that turned out to be false positives on inspection: the named commits never touched the code being critiqued, so these were fresh findings on original round-0 code surfaced by Copilot's cumulative full-file review, not fixes gone wrong. The batch's real cascade is narrower: a test-writing fix (F5, round 1) left both a hardcoded-sample coupling flaw (F6) and a not-actually-type-level exhaustiveness claim (F8) for later rounds to catch, and a behavior-tightening fix (F7, round 2) left the PR description undocumented until round 4 (F10).
guidance_observations: Several ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags in this PR were false positives: Copilot's per-round full-file review resurfaced pre-existing defects (empty-key routing, boolean-falsy documentation, uncached theme lookup) that the named fix commit never touched -- worth filtering these out when tuning guidance from cascade data.
The two genuine cascades both trace to a fix that wrote something durable (a test, a PR description) without making it fully correct or keeping it in sync with a later code change in the same commit.
